experiments.question: Which runtime facts about time zones can ADR-002 rely on in Node.js 24, and so in the web app's Vitest runs: Temporal, London's clock-change days, quarter-hour offsets, en-GB formats, the ambient zone under TZ, the instant string form?
experiments.finding: Node.js 24.18 (tz 2026b) has no global Temporal. London's 2026-10-25 and 2027-10-31 are 25 hours and 2027-03-28 is 23 hours; quarter-hour instants of those days give 100 slots with 01:00 to 01:45 twice (BST, then GMT) and 92 slots with no 01:xx. No zone among 418 has an offset that is not a multiple of 15 minutes in 2026 to 2028. en-GB writes '02:00 to 03:00 (09:00 to 10:00 in Jakarta)', 'Thu 5 Nov', GMT and BST (en-US gives GMT+1). TZ=Asia/Kolkata sets the ambient zone and resolves as 'Asia/Calcutta'. toISOString writes 2026-11-05T02:00:00.000Z; a string without a zone parses as local time. London's changes are 147 to 217 days apart; the next after 2026-10-31 is 2027-03-28, 148 days ahead.

experiments.question: Does storing booking times as instants in PostgreSQL 17 hold PRD v2 AC-5.3's touching rule and AC-4.2's day query with no zone in SQL?
experiments.finding: PostgreSQL 17.11: timestamptz reads back the same epoch whatever the session TimeZone, while a timestamp column given '...Z' reads back 7 hours apart under Asia/Jakarta and Europe/London sessions. tstzrange '[)' ranges that touch do not overlap; an EXCLUDE USING gist (room WITH =, tstzrange(start_at, end_at, '[)') WITH &&) constraint (btree_gist ships in postgres:17-alpine) refuses an overlap with 23P01 whose DETAIL names one conflicting row. London's 25-hour 2027-10-31 queried as two instants returns the bookings at both ends of the local day.

routed.text: booking-api@v1 is in ADR-002's affects: its front matter needs governed_by: [ADR-001, ADR-002] (and the body's Governed by line), or gate C3 errors once the file exists. ADR-002 fixes for it: every instant, request and response, is a UTC string in toISOString form (2026-11-05T02:00:00.000Z), never a local time or another offset; the rooms-on-a-date query takes the day as two instants and returns each room's bookings overlapping that half-open range, earliest first; each room carries timeZone (IANA) and its office's name; a booking occupies [start, end), so touching bookings do not overlap; start and end must have UTC minutes a multiple of 15 and zero seconds and milliseconds, end after start; 'started' means the backend's clock reads the start or later (refused for booking, and a booking can be cancelled only while the clock is before its start); my bookings are those whose end is after the backend's clock, soonest first; the overlap refusal carries the room's name and the other booking's start and end as instants, so the web app writes AC-5.3's message.

Two choices ADR-002 leaves to the draft. (1) How far ahead: London's clock changes are 147 to 217 days apart and the next after 2026-10-31 is 2027-03-28 (148 days); with a smaller limit, the integration node cannot always book on the next change day through the API under the real clock (ADR-002 Consequences), so state the limit with that in view, or say how the change-day criteria are reached. (2) Which other booking the overlap refusal names when a request overlaps several: an exclusion constraint's 23P01 DETAIL names one conflicting row (hsdd/auto/experiments/time-model-postgres/), so the contract should pick a rule, for example the earliest, and the producer re-reads it.

ADR-002 item 3: the profile serves the account's zone as timeZone, an IANA name (ayu Asia/Jakarta, budi Europe/London), and the web app may use no other zone, so it shows no booking time without it. An optional field under additive-only leaves a consumer nothing to fall back on; the touch should state that the producer always sends it for the built-in accounts, or weigh that in its classification (DEC-007 anticipated this). profile-api@v2's governed_by and body line already read [ADR-001, ADR-002] (DEC-036); the touch need not add them.

ADR-002's affects names simple-login (DEC-035), and the root header and its three embedded summaries now carry ADR-002 under Governed by (simple-login.integration's for the first time); keep those lines when restating the header, or gate C3 errors. A Decisions bullet for ADR-002 can say: instants on the wire and in PostgreSQL, the account's IANA zone, the web app converts and formats, the backend's clock decides.

ADR-002 for the backend's plan: start and end as timestamptz with the half-open overlap rule; an exclusion constraint on tstzrange(start_at, end_at, '[)') with btree_gist is one way to hold AC-5.4, but its 23P01 DETAIL names one row, so the AC-5.3 body needs a re-read (hsdd/auto/experiments/time-model-postgres/); no zone arithmetic in the service; the quarter-hour check on the UTC instant; the injected clock decides started and ended (start equal to now is started); the account data gains timeZone; the gate's tests run with TZ set to a zone that is neither account's nor UTC.

ADR-002 for the web app's plan: one module of pure functions taking the zone as an argument (instant to wall time, a date to [start of date, start of next date), the form's quarter-hour instants, the repeated-hour and other-date marks), tested in isolation on 2027-03-28 (23 hours, 92 slots, no 01:xx) and 2027-10-31 (25 hours, 100 slots, 01:00 to 01:45 twice as BST then GMT) per hsdd/auto/experiments/time-model-intl/; Node.js 24 has no global Temporal, so use Intl or a library on it, or a polyfill; en-GB gives 'Thu 5 Nov', HH:mm with hourCycle h23, GMT and BST (en-US gives GMT+1); Vitest runs with TZ set to a third zone; the browser's clock only picks the Rooms screen's opening date; the overlap message is built from the refusal's instants, not from error.message.

ADR-002 for the integration plan: the browser tests run with the browser's time zone set to a zone that is neither account's nor UTC (for example Asia/Kolkata, +05:30); the change-day tests take the next last Sunday of March and of October after the real clock, never a fixed date (2026-10-25 has passed; the next is 2027-03-28), and booking-api@v1's how-far-ahead limit decides whether that day is bookable through the API; the backend's clock decides 'started', which an end-to-end test cannot set, so the plan says which scripted test covers AC-5.5 and AC-6.2's started case (PRD v2 Success); the strings to assert are ADR-002 item 7's, including '23:00 to Fri 6 Nov 02:00' and '01:30 BST' / '01:30 GMT'.
